findings.title: website_name include predicate is misnamed and bypasses untrusted-user hiding
findings.body: The conditional is defined as include_website_name instead of the include_website_name? convention used by ActiveModel Serializers and by the other predicates in this file, so it is never invoked and website_name is always serialized. Additionally, :website_name is absent from untrusted_attributes, which hides :website for TL0 users viewed anonymously. Anonymous visitors therefore receive the host and path derived from a website that was intended to be hidden, and profiles without a website also gain a spurious website_name: nil key.

findings.title: Same-domain check is asymmetric for apex and www hosts
findings.body: When the website is http://www.example.com/me and the instance is example.com, the hosts have different label counts, so execution reaches the final branch, which only checks whether the instance host ends with the website host. That check fails and only www.example.com is shown. The reverse configuration, website example.com/me on instance www.example.com, does return example.com/me. The common apex/www combination is therefore handled inconsistently and the requested full path is not shown.

findings.title: Stripping the first host label falsely matches domains under public suffixes
findings.body: The sibling-subdomain branch assumes the registrable domain is always the last two labels. For example, website example.co.uk/user and an unrelated instance at other.co.uk both reduce to co.uk after removing the first label, so the serializer incorrectly displays example.co.uk/user as though the website belonged to the instance domain. The same false positive applies to other multi-part public suffixes and shared suffixes such as github.io.

findings.title: Displayed website text drops query string and fragment
findings.body: For a matching domain the display text is built from URI#path only. A website such as http://example.com/user?tab=posts#details is displayed as example.com/user even though the actual link points to the full URL, so the supposedly complete URL shown to readers is truncated and can misrepresent the destination, particularly for URLs whose identity is in the query string.

findings.title: New website_name branches and visibility rules are untested
findings.body: The added examples cover only an unrelated two-label domain, an exact host match, and a website that is the parent of the instance host. They do not exercise the equal-length sibling-subdomain branch, the apex-versus-www case, a blank or malformed website, or serialization of website_name for a TL0 user viewed anonymously; the untrusted_attributes list in the TL0 context is also unchanged. The untested include predicate and subdomain logic can therefore regress, or leak the hidden website, without any spec failing.
